title: Texture2D node in the shader editor outputs incorrect color when plugging in UV values 0.0 or 1.0
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: v4.3.stable.official [77dcf97d8], v4.5.1.stable.official [f62fdbde1]

### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated Radeon RX 590 Series (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 31.0.21921.1000) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-8500 CPU @ 3.00GHz (6 threads) - 15.92 GiB memory

### Issue description

When plugging in a value of 0.0 or 1.0 into the UV input of a Texture2D node, then plugging the Color output into the Albedo, the Texture2D node seems to be sampled at X coordinate 0.5, HOWEVER when inspecting the color in the editor (using the eye icon) the color is as expected.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a 3D Scene
2. Add a `MeshInstance3D` node
3. For the Mesh, select any pre-existing mesh
4. Create a new material override on the mesh
5. Add a VisualShader for the Material
6. Create a `Texture2D` node
7. Add a `GradientTexture1D` to the `Texture2D` node
8. Create a `FloatConstant` Node
9. Plug `FloatConstant` into the UV of the `Texture2D` node
10. Open the preview of the Texture2D node
11. Cycle the float values between 0.0 and 1.0 (overshooting is not a problem)
12. Observe as the mesh is 0.5 gray at 0.0 and 1.0, but the node preview show proper black/white

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[mrp-texture-2d.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24845970/mrp-texture-2d.zip)
